findings.message: `return void <expression>;` folds two statements into one: it runs the expression, throws its value away, and exits. Write the expression as its own statement, then `return;`. The `void` operator is how this codebase marks a promise dropped on purpose, so spending it to squeeze a `console.log` into a return makes the reader stop and work out which of the two is meant, and it hides a second statement inside a line that looks like an exit.
